I believe you're talking about minimum wage. Minimum wage in economic terms is a price floor on the price of labor. Price floors are never good because they artificially and arbitrarily set a minimum price on a good/service. When you take emotion out of the argument, labor is nothing more than a service that is provided by a worker. If there is a price floor on labor it will skew the price of low end labor and employers will not employ workers that produce less value than that of price floor. Essentially you arbitrarily price certain workers out of the labor market.

I understand what you're saying, that raising the price of labor will allow workers to be better able to purchase goods. While this may be true, you still end up pricing certain workers out of the job market. Now instead of two workers that could potentially save up to purchase a product there is one potential customer that will have to save less to purchase a product. Automation is also a concern. If the price of labor vs. putting an RFID tag on all groceries is beneficial due to mandated price increases on labor, you're going to end up with a bunch of RFID tags on groceries and fewer people employed.

Government has no business arbitrarily mandating the price of anything. Minimum wage is nothing more than a tool to buy votes from the economically illiterate and emotional voters. Just like separation of church and state we need a separation of economy and state.
